notes.title: Thank You for Your Support. Introducing Our Next Challenge: Animas!
notes.content:
Greetings, Mechanophagia community!

We have exciting news to share! We’ve just officially announced our new project: [b]Animas[/b]. While it’s very different from Mechanophagia, we’re confident many of you will find this game equally captivating. Ready to learn more?

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3325720/Animas/

We want to deeply thank everyone who has supported us by playing, commenting on, and sharing Mechanophagia. Your encouragement inspires us to keep improving and creating even more ambitious projects! That’s why [b]we have a small request[/b]: if you’re intrigued by what we’re crafting with Animas, don’t forget to [b]add it to your Steam wishlist[/b]! Every wishlist and recommendation helps us reach more players like you.

This is just the beginning of an exciting journey, and we’d love for you to [b]join us from the very start[/b]. Your support and enthusiasm are our biggest motivation to keep pushing forward!

Thank you for continuing to believe in our work. 🚀

Stay tuned for more updates!

— The Apamate Studio Team

notes.title: Update notes - Version 1.0.2
notes.content:
We have made a small update to Mechanophagia. These are some of the changes we have made:

[list]
[*] We added the icons for some missing achievements (both in the game and in the Steam library).
[*]We modified a little bit the background of the first level, to give a little more contrast to the scene and better distinguish what is happening.
[*]We also modified the colors of the main character, to make them more vibrant, and we improved the visual effect when receiving damage.
[*]We have made some balance changes to several enemies, based on what we have seen from the first players of the game. We will continue to analyze all the data we get, and improve what is needed.
[*]We fixed some small bugs in the English localization of the game, with texts that did not appear in the correct language.
[/list]

notes.title: Mechanophagia is now available!
notes.content:
Finally [b]Mechanophagia[/b] is out, after almost a year of development, and we are very happy to finally share the result of our work. We are a small Venezuelan studio, formed by two brothers, and this is the first videogame we publish, but it will not be the last.

Let's start by reviewing the content of the game at the time of its release:

[list]
[*] 3 different levels, each one with its own enemies with different behaviors, and a unique boss after surviving for 10 minutes.
[*] 56 random upgrade cards during the runs.
[*] 6 permanent upgrades, that you can assign with achievement points between games, and that you can reassign at any time.
[*] 39 different achievements, with which you will earn points to buy more permanent upgrades.
[/list]

[h2]What will be released in the coming weeks[/h2]

One thing we want to clarify is that Mechanophagia has not been released in early access. Our plan has always been that Mechanophagia would be a small game, that would serve us to learn the necessary skills for the development of a videogame, and that we could apply those skills to our future projects. Even so, the game could not be ready for the release date in the conditions we would have liked. Partly because of our inexperience as developers, and partly because the climate of political instability in our country has made it difficult for us to work this last month.

Therefore, during the next few weeks we will be updating the game, until we get it to the state in which we wanted it to be released. These are the things we will be adding or improving in the next weeks:

[list]
[*] Quick mode (5 minute games, to get to the boss faster)
[*] Visual improvements to many parts of the game
[*] A better transition to the boss fight, and a more satisfying victory screen.
[*] Add many sound effects missing in the game.
[*] Difficulty balancing.
[/list]

[h2]Things we could add later[/h2]

Throughout the development of Mechanophagia we have been having to put ideas aside, as we understood the difficulties involved. Many of these ideas require time and resources to bring to fruition, so we cannot guarantee that they will ever come to fruition. They will depend largely on the results of the game, the number of people who buy it and the feedback we receive.

[list]
[*] Localization to other languages. It will also depend on the results we are getting, the countries where the game is most played, or what we are asked for more often.
[*] Different music for each level, or for the battles against bosses.
[*] New random upgrades, with more unique effects that alter the gameplay of the run more significantly.
[*] Another progress system between games (a kind of deck, that allows you to block some upgrades from appearing in the run).
[*] Endless mode, with enemies from all levels.
[/list]

[h2]Things that almost definitely will NOT be done[/h2]

Finally, even if the game turns out to be a bigger success than we expect, there are some things we are almost certain we will NOT do. Developing Mechanophagia has been a very enriching experience, but we want to carry that experience into new projects. Therefore, it is almost certain that Mechanophagia will not have:

[list]
[*] New characters
[*] New levels
[*] New enemies
[/list]


Thank you very much for your interest in Mechanophagia. If you want to know more about the progress of this, and future projects of our studio, feel free to visit us at [url=https://discord.gg/njmgmMrHAD]our discord[/url].

Translated with DeepL.com (free version)

notes.title: Meet the world of Mechanophagia!
notes.content:
Mechanophagia is a bullet hell with roguelite elements where you play as Tetsuo, a brave robot who must defend his city from the attack of an alien species that feeds on machines. This horde of metal-eating aliens is known among robots as mechanophages.

Born of flesh in a world dominated by metal, the mechanophages are flesh-and-blood beings who decided to leave their carnivorous nature behind and consume machines to transcend their bodies' natural limits. Since food was scarce in their environment and nuclear energy was abundant, they saw in machines a tempting possibility to obtain the energy necessary to survive. A forced symbiosis with various machines allowed them to metabolize nuclear energy, but amid the frenzy, they destroyed their own means of production. Now they roam the galaxy looking for synthetic life forms that have advanced enough in the production of nuclear fusion energy to feed on them.

The idea for the world of Mechanophagia was born mainly from this idea of grotesque beings that feed on machines. "Tetsuo: The Iron Man" our most direct inspiration, we wanted to imagine what the opposite would be like; instead of the machine consuming the flesh, the flesh consuming the machine. Another big inspiration was Akira, its neon city, and, mainly that scene where the power consumes Tetsuo and he becomes a grotesque mass of flesh and wires. We want to bring some elements of body horror seen from the perspective of a robot, and thus achieve an aesthetic that is both captivating and a bit distressing.

[b]Add Mechanophagia to your wishlist so you can find out about the launch, and enjoy this world and the story of Tetsuo, the first to rise.[/b]
